description: AutoCAD drawings through AutoCAD's own COM (ActiveX) API: structured operations, never mouse clicks or typed commands. Coordinates are drawing units; points are {"x", "y", "z"} objects (z defaults to 0). Every tool works on the ACTIVE document's model space. Every state-changing tool reads its result back from AutoCAD and fails with VERIFICATION_FAILED if it does not match.

tools.name: autocad.status
tools.description: Report whether AutoCAD is installed, registered for COM, running and answering COM, plus its open drawings. Never starts AutoCAD. ready=true means the autocad.* tools can work now (AutoCAD answering COM) or after autocad.launch (installed, COM-registered, not running).

tools.name: autocad.launch
tools.description: Start AutoCAD (or attach to the running instance) and wait until it answers COM and is idle. Startup can take minutes. Verified: COM answers and AutoCAD reports itself quiescent. A fresh AutoCAD usually has NO open drawing: call autocad.new_document next.

launched.description: true: started by this call; false: attached to a running AutoCAD.

tools.name: autocad.new_document
tools.description: Create a new drawing (optionally from a .dwt template) and make it the active document. Verified: the document count increased and the new drawing is active.

template.description: Absolute path to a .dwt, or a template file name AutoCAD resolves from its template folder (e.g. 'acad.dwt'). Default: configured template, else AutoCAD's default.

tools.name: autocad.list_documents
tools.description: List the open drawings: name, full path (empty if never saved), whether all changes are saved, and which one is active.

tools.name: autocad.get_entities
tools.description: Read entities from the active drawing's model space with their handle, object_name (e.g. AcDbLine, AcDbCircle, AcDbPolyline, AcDbText), layer and geometry. Filters are case-insensitive; object_name accepts 'circle' or 'AcDbCircle'.

tools.name: autocad.create_line
tools.description: Draw a line in model space. layer must already exist (autocad.create_layer); default is the current layer. Verified by reading the line back by handle; a mismatching line is erased and VERIFICATION_FAILED is returned. Undo with autocad.erase.

tools.name: autocad.create_circle
tools.description: Draw a circle in model space. layer must already exist (autocad.create_layer); default is the current layer. Verified by reading the circle back by handle; a mismatching circle is erased and VERIFICATION_FAILED is returned. Undo with autocad.erase.

tools.name: autocad.create_polyline
tools.description: Draw a 2D lightweight polyline through the points (all points must share the same z, used as the polyline's elevation). closed=true joins the last point to the first. layer must already exist. Verified by reading the vertices back by handle; a mismatch is erased and VERIFICATION_FAILED is returned. Undo with autocad.erase.

tools.name: autocad.create_text
tools.description: Place single-line text (left-aligned at the insertion point). layer must already exist. Verified by reading text, insertion point, height and rotation back by handle; a mismatch is erased and VERIFICATION_FAILED is returned. Undo with autocad.erase.

tools.name: autocad.create_layer
tools.description: Create a layer in the active drawing (an existing layer is reused). color is an AutoCAD Color Index 1-255 (1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 cyan, 5 blue, 6 magenta, 7 white/black). Verified: the layer exists afterwards with the requested color.

tools.name: autocad.verify_geometry
tools.description: Read-only check that the entity with this handle exists in the active drawing and matches the expected properties within the configured geometry tolerance. Use it in task.complete checks with {"matches": true}. A missing entity returns matches=false (not an error).

tools.name: autocad.save
tools.description: Save the active drawing as a .dwg (configured DWG version) at an absolute path; missing parent folders are created. Replacing a different existing file needs overwrite=true. Verified: the file exists, is non-empty and the drawing is now associated with that path.

tools.name: autocad.export_dxf
tools.description: Write a copy of the active drawing (as it is now, including unsaved changes) as an ASCII .dxf at an absolute path. The drawing must already have been saved as .dwg (call autocad.save first), otherwise CONFLICT; it stays associated with that .dwg. Replacing an existing file needs overwrite=true. Verified: the file exists, is non-empty, starts like a DXF in the configured DXF version, and the drawing's path is still the .dwg.

tools.name: autocad.export_pdf
tools.description: Plot the active layout's drawing extents, scaled to fit and centred, to a PDF with the configured plot device. The layout's plot settings are restored afterwards. Replacing an existing file needs overwrite=true. Verified: the file exists, is non-empty and starts with %PDF.

tools.name: autocad.zoom_extents
tools.description: Zoom the active drawing's view to show everything (view change only; geometry is untouched).

tools.name: autocad.erase
tools.description: Erase one entity of the active drawing by handle. Verified: the handle no longer resolves to a live entity.

tools.name: autocad.draw_floor_plan
tools.description: Draw a complete, professional single-storey house floor plan (mặt bằng nhà cấp 4) in ONE call: the layout is computed for you (porch, living room, corridor, bedrooms with en-suite bathrooms, shared bathroom, laundry, kitchen-dining, altar room, study, storage as the size allows), walls with real thickness (filled), doors with swing arcs, windows, furniture, room names with areas, dimensions, title and an area table, on layers KT-*. Units are metres. Give width and depth of the footprint (or the area). Use this for ANY request to draw a house / floor plan / mặt bằng instead of drawing walls with lines; afterwards add details with the other autocad.* tools if asked. AutoCAD must be running (autocad.launch). new_document=true (default) draws in a fresh drawing. floors=1 (default) draws the single-storey plan exactly as before. floors 2-4: one plan per floor (floor n to the left of floor 1, 22 m + width apart) with the stair symbol, riser lines, walking line (LEN/XUONG), the slab opening on the floors above and a roof plan; floors above repeat the ground-floor walls (ASSUMED), exterior doors become windows. Stair sizes not given are ASSUMED working defaults; limits are applied only from a verified profile. Idempotent: every entity carries XData (application LGA_OP) with a marker derived from the operation inputs (or idempotency_key); an identical second call in the same drawing finds them and adds nothing (if_exists=skip, default) or erases and redraws them (replace). (a repeat in the SAME drawing, i.e. new_document=false.)

width.description: footprint width along the street, m

area.description: footprint area in m², when width/depth are not both given

floors.description: number of floors, 1 to 4 (default 1 = the single-storey house exactly as before). Pass the SAME value to every tool of the set.

floor_heights.description: clear floor-to-ceiling height of each floor, m (one per floor; default storey_height for all, ASSUMED). Floor n is at the previous ceiling + slab_thickness.

stair.description: stair settings for floors >= 2. Riser count = ceil(floor-to-floor height / riser_target), riser height = height / count (recomputed, never typed). Anything not given is an ASSUMED working default, not a code limit.

landing.description: landing depth between the two flights, m (default = width)

flights.description: 2 = U stair with a landing (default; stacks over 2-4 floors); 1 = straight (2 floors only)

headroom.description: clear height assumed above the flight to size the slab opening, m (default 2.0, ASSUMED)

room.description: kind of room that gets the stair (default living)

position.description: lower-left corner of the stair footprint in plan metres; default: first clear corner of the room

profile.description: limits from the Project Standards Profile: {max_riser_height | min_tread_depth | min_stair_width: {value, verified_by, source}}. A limit is applied (and checked by COORD.STAIR_RISERS) ONLY when verified_by names who verified it; otherwise it is reported as ASSUMED and not applied.

storey_height.description: clear floor-to-ceiling height, m (default 3.3, ASSUMED working default, not a code value)

plinth_height.description: floor level above the outside ground, m (default 0.45, ASSUMED)

slab_thickness.description: graphic ceiling/roof slab thickness, m (default 0.1, ASSUMED; no structural design)

roof_slope_deg.description: pitched roof slope in degrees (default 30, ASSUMED)

window_sill.description: window sill height above the floor, m (default 0.9, ASSUMED)

roof_plan.description: floors >= 2: also draw the roof plan to the left of the top floor plan

layer_map.description: office layer names: {"A-WALL-EXT": "MY-WALL", ...}; standard A-* names are used for any layer not listed

if_exists.description: what to do when entities of an identical earlier call are already in the drawing (found by their LGA_OP XData marker): skip = draw nothing and verify they are all there (default), replace = erase them and draw again, error = refuse

idempotency_key.description: optional operation id used as the marker instead of the hash of the inputs: calls with the same key share their entities

tools.name: autocad.draw_image
tools.description: Draw a PICTURE or PHOTO in AutoCAD as a coloured pencil SKETCH in ONE call: AutoCAD only has lines, so the picture is drawn the way a person sketches it - the outline of every colour region plus shading hatch lines inside the darker ones, and every stroke in the colour of the thing it describes (each colour on its own layer SKETCH-RRGGBB). Maximum detail by default (hundreds of contours, thousands of shading lines, up to 48 colours). Give the picture's file path (attachments are listed under 'Files the user attached'). new_document=true (default) draws in a fresh drawing; paper='white' (default) makes the model-space background white so dark pencil lines are visible. Use this for 'vẽ lại ảnh này trong AutoCAD', 'ký họa', 'sketch this picture'. Do not use autocad.create_line for a picture. It leaves the drawing open and unsaved: do NOT save, export or zoom afterwards unless the user asked for a file (the tool already zooms to the sketch).

detail.description: Leave at 'max'; lower only when the user asks for a quick or rough sketch.

shading.description: Hatch the non-light regions (false: contours only).

tools.name: autocad.profile_check
tools.description: Check a Project Standards Profile (locality, authority, house type, floors, units, coordinate system, paper, scale, layer convention, area rule, codes) before drawing. Lists what is missing, assumed, invalid or legally unverified and returns clarification questions with suggested options, a multi-select flag, 'Khac' and 'Giu UNKNOWN'. Never fills a missing value and never suggests legal requirements. Offline; does not need AutoCAD.

profile.description: Field id -> value, or {value, status PROVIDED|ASSUMED|UNKNOWN, verified_by}. Omit for an empty profile (all questions).

tools.name: autocad.validate_model
tools.description: Run the drawing validation rules (rule_id, scope, severity BLOCKER/ERROR/WARNING/INFO, result PASS/FAIL/WARN/NOT_RUN with evidence) over an intermediate model: units, zero-length segments, open or self-intersecting boundaries, duplicate entities, walls without thickness, doors/windows without a host wall, duplicate door codes, schedule vs symbols, dimension override vs geometry (CONFLICT), area recomputed from the boundary, stair risers vs height, level consistency. Give exactly one of model, model_path (JSON file) or autocad_entities (the entities array from autocad.get_entities). Tolerances are per purpose in mm. Any open BLOCKER or ERROR makes overall FAIL; rules lacking data are NOT_RUN. Offline; does not need AutoCAD and does not change any drawing.

model.description: {meta, entities[], schedules, profile}; entity schema: entity_id, entity_type, geometry, units, level_id, elevation, properties, relationships, source, status.

model_path.description: Absolute path of a JSON file holding the model.

autocad_entities.description: Entities as returned by autocad.get_entities; types are inferred only from standard layer names.

layer_map.description: Standard layer name -> office layer name.

tolerances.description: Purpose -> mm (or {value, unit: mm|drawing}); area_rel and scale_rel are ratios.

rule_params.description: rule_id -> parameters, e.g. COORD.STAIR_RISERS {max_riser_height} only from a verified profile.

waivers.description: {rule_id, approved_by, reason, date, scope, entity_ids?}; BLOCKERs cannot be waived.

tools.name: autocad.compare_revisions
tools.description: Compare two entity sets (old, new; optional common base) by id, geometry, layer, properties and relationships into added / modified / deleted / conflicted, with possible id renames. When ids barely overlap the mapping is flagged uncertain and a mass deletion is marked as needing confirmation. Optional log builds revision-log rows (reason, source request, actor, sheets). Offline; changes nothing.

tools.name: autocad.plan_operation
tools.description: Dry-run check of a planned AutoCAD operation: returns its idempotency key and entity marker (a retry with the same inputs is recognised, not repeated) and whether it needs explicit confirmation (bulk delete over the threshold, purge, explode, unit/scale change, layer-structure change, overwriting an existing file). Changes nothing.

tools.name: autocad.report
tools.description: Build the run report with sections INPUT_REVIEW, ASSUMPTIONS, QUESTIONS, DRAWING_PLAN, EXECUTION_LOG, VALIDATION, OPEN_ISSUES, OUTPUTS, FINAL_STATUS, LIMITATIONS. FINAL_STATUS is computed only from verified evidence (DRAFT, CAD_VALID, DRAWING_CHECKED, COORDINATED, CODE_REVIEWED): output files are listed only if they exist on disk, evidence flags (dwg_opened_in_autocad, pdf_rendered_checked) must be set only when a prior tool result proved them, and a construction-issue status is impossible without a human code-review file and an approval file. Optional model/model_path/autocad_entities is validated first. report_path (.md) also writes a .json twin. Never claims compliance; lists what was NOT checked.

evidence.description: dwg_opened_in_autocad, pdf_rendered_checked, autocad_session: true only when a prior tool result proved it. dwg_reopen_check: the object data.reopen_check of autocad.reopen_check (the saved DWG was closed and opened again in AutoCAD and entity counts compared); when present, dwg_opened_in_autocad is DERIVED from it, not taken from the flag.

code_review_file.description: Absolute path of a JSON file written by the human reviewer: reviewer, role, date, scope.

issue_approval_file.description: Absolute path of a JSON file: approved_by, role, date, document_ref.

report_path.description: Absolute .md path to write (a .json twin is written next to it).

tools.name: autocad.house_model
tools.description: Build the shared house data model (levels, wall runs with thickness and centre line, doors and windows with unique codes, sizes, sill heights and host walls, rooms with boundary and area, roof, assumptions) WITHOUT touching AutoCAD, and return it in the intermediate-model format of autocad.validate_model / autocad.report (data.model). The model is computed from the SAME parameters as autocad.draw_floor_plan (width, depth/area, bedrooms, altar, study, porch), so pass the same values to every view tool: plan, elevations, sections and schedules then agree (codes D1.., W1.., sizes, levels, areas). Vertical numbers that are not given (storey height, plinth, sill, door/window heights, roof) are working defaults flagged ASSUMED; nothing here checks any building code. Pass `views` (the data.views / data.view records returned by autocad.draw_elevation, draw_section, draw_schedules) to include what was actually drawn, so the cross-view rules can compare plan, elevations, sections and schedule tables; without them those rules report NOT_RUN. export_path writes the model as .json (backup before overwrite). Floors 1-4 (floors, floor_heights, stair, profile): levels per floor, stairs with risers recomputed from the floor-to-floor height, slab openings, per-floor codes; limits are applied only from a verified profile, everything else is flagged ASSUMED. layouts/sheet_index/pdf_render_check/reopen_check carry the measured sheet and plot evidence for the PLOT.* and FILE.REOPEN_COUNTS rules.

tools.description: Draw one or more elevations (front, rear, left, right) of the house in AutoCAD from the shared house model: ground line, floor levels with +0.000 datum labels, walls, roof, porch posts, every door and window of that facade (same codes, sizes and sills as the plan and the schedules) with code tags, level marks and dimensions, on the standard layers A-* (A-WALL-EXT, A-DOOR, A-WINDOW, A-GLAZING, A-ROOF, A-ANNO-LEVEL, A-DIMS ...), model space 1:1, everything ByLayer. tools.name: autocad.draw_stair
tools.description: Draw the stair symbol of one floor of a multi-storey house from the shared house model: outline, one line per riser face, landing edge, walking line with arrow and the text LEN (stair that starts on this floor) or XUONG (stair that arrives), and on floors >= 2 the outline of the slab opening above the stair below (layers A-STAIR, A-HIDDEN, A-ANNO-TEXT, model space 1:1, ByLayer). The same parameters as autocad.house_model (width, depth/area, bedrooms ..., floors >= 2, floor_heights, stair, profile) give the same stair: riser count = ceil(floor-to-floor height / riser_target), riser height recomputed = height / count, tread, width, landing, headroom from the arguments or ASSUMED working defaults; a limit (max_riser_height, min_tread_depth, min_stair_width) is applied only from a profile entry with verified_by. The symbol is placed at the origin of that floor's plan (floor n is drawn to the left of floor 1 by autocad.draw_floor_plan, which already calls this for every floor). data.view is the record measured from the drawing (riser lines counted, openings read back); give it to autocad.house_model (views). Idempotent: every entity carries XData (application LGA_OP) with a marker derived from the operation inputs (or idempotency_key); an identical second call in the same drawing finds them and adds nothing (if_exists=skip, default) or erases and redraws them (replace).

tools.name: autocad.create_layout
tools.description: Create the paper-space layouts of the drawing set of a house, one per sheet, named by sheet code (spec section 12: A-101 plan floor 1, A-102.. further floors, next code roof plan, A-201..A-204 elevations, A-301 section, A-501 door/window tables, A-503 room tables; the codes are configurable with sheet_codes). Each layout gets the paper size and orientation (A4-A1, landscape/portrait, PDF plot device, mm), a frame, a title block and ONE viewport at an exact 1:N scale (requested per kind or sheet code in scales, default 1:100, tables 1:50; the largest standard scale that fits is used and reported when the content does not fit), centred on the sheet's model-space window and LOCKED. Title block fields: project, client, designer, date, revision, status come only from title_block; sheet code, sheet name and scale are written by the tool; prepared / checked / approved and signatures are NEVER written (drawn as empty cells; asking for them is refused). Everything is read back from AutoCAD (paper, rotation, viewport scale, lock, title block texts) into data.layouts / data.sheet_index for autocad.house_model and the PLOT.* rules. Draw the views first (autocad.draw_floor_plan, draw_elevation, draw_section, draw_schedules; pass their data.views as views to use the real extents). The model is in metres, so 1:100 means 10 mm of paper per drawing unit. Idempotent: every entity carries XData (application LGA_OP) with a marker derived from the operation inputs (or idempotency_key); an identical second call in the same drawing finds them and adds nothing (if_exists=skip, default) or erases and redraws them (replace).

tools.name: autocad.plot_sheets
tools.description: Plot the layouts made by autocad.create_layout to ONE multi-page PDF (the PDF plot device, one page per sheet, in the order given by sheets or by sheet code), then check the PDF: PyMuPDF in a SYSTEM Python renders every page to an image (non-blank), counts the pages against the sheets, checks the page size against the layout paper and looks for the sheet code in each page's text. If AutoCAD wrote a different number of pages the sheets are plotted one by one and merged. When no Python with PyMuPDF is found the PDF is NOT rendered and data.pdf_render_check is null: say so, do not claim the PDF was checked. An existing file needs overwrite=true (backup first, restored if the plot fails); the operation is recorded. Plot settings changed for the plot (BACKGROUNDPLOT, QuietErrorMode) are restored. Give data.pdf_render_check to autocad.house_model for PLOT.PDF_PAGES_MATCH_SHEETS.

sheets.description: layout (sheet) names in page order; default: every layout made by autocad.create_layout, in natural order

render_check.description: render and inspect the PDF with PyMuPDF (system Python)

png_dir.description: folder for one PNG per page (optional)

tools.name: autocad.reopen_check
tools.description: Evidence that a saved DWG opens: count the entities of the open drawing at path (model space by object type, marked entities, layouts with entity counts, paper size and viewport scale/lock), close it (refused with CONFLICT while it has unsaved changes: save first), open the DWG from disk in AutoCAD again, count again and compare. Only the drawing at path is closed, and only after a save; with keep_open=false (default) the re-opened drawing is closed again (read-only), with keep_open=true it stays open for editing. If the drawing was not open, expected_counts (a previous data.after) is compared instead. data.evidence goes to autocad.report: dwg_opened_in_autocad becomes true only when the re-open succeeded AND every count is equal. data.reopen_check goes to autocad.house_model (FILE.REOPEN_COUNTS).

expected_counts.description: counts to compare with when the drawing is not open (data.after of an earlier call)

handle.description: Entity handle (hex), as returned by create_* or get_entities.
